# SPHEREx Explorer

SPHEREx Explorer is a web-based project developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 – Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Its main aim is to make astronomical data easier to access, understand and explore through an interactive platform.

SPHEREx is a NASA space telescope that surveys the universe using infrared light across 102 spectral bands. Our website aims to provide users with a simple way to explore these observations and understand changes in different regions of the sky.

The platform includes four major features: **Explore the Sky**, where users can search using Right Ascension (RA), Declination (Dec) and search radius; **Image Comparison**, which allows users to compare observations of the same sky region; **Observation History**, which displays available observation dates; and **Infrared Explorer**, which helps users explore different infrared bands.

We are developing the website using Bolt.new, React, HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with plans to integrate genuine NASA/IPAC SPHEREx archive data and use Python with Astropy for FITS image processing.

Our current challenge is connecting to NASA's archive because its TAP and SIA services have returned server errors. We are preparing alternative data-access methods.

**Our vision is to make infrared astronomy more accessible through an interactive platform that encourages exploration, comparison and scientific discovery.**
details:
What It Does & How It Works The SPHEREx Astronomy Explorer is an interactive web application designed to help students, educators, and space enthusiasts explore NASA’s SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer) mission. Users can navigate through mission objectives, inspect near-infrared spectroscopy concepts, and interactively explore how SPHEREx maps hundreds of millions of galaxies and searches for water and organic molecules across the Milky Way.

Benefits & Intended Impact Scientific data and mission documentation for space telescopes are often dense and difficult for non-specialists to digest. Our application bridges that gap by turning complex astrophysical concepts—such as cosmic inflation, the Epoch of Reionization, and interstellar ice surveys—into a visual, self-guided experience. Its intended impact is to democratize access to NASA mission science and inspire STEM engagement among students and citizen scientists.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

  • Frontend & UI: React, TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, and Tailwind CSS
  • Build Tool & Hosting: Vite, developed and deployed via Bolt ([https://spherex-astronomy-da-ox4u.bolt.host](https://spherex-astronomy-da-ox4u.bolt.host))
  • Scientific Reference: Official NASA/JPL SPHEREx mission parameters and publicly available mission datasets

Creativity & Design Considerations Rather than presenting static text walls, we designed an intuitive, dark-mode space interface that mirrors the visual feel of astronomical observation tools. Key factors our team considered included:

  • Accessibility & Clarity: Breaking down technical spectroscopy terms into clear, digestible visual modules without losing scientific accuracy.
  • Responsiveness & Performance: Ensuring the web app loads quickly and works smoothly across both desktop and mobile browsers without requiring users to install heavy software.
